# Job Chapter 30 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 427r–427v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_030_page_001.jpg, JOB_030_page_002.jpg

---

**30:1** "But-now they-mock [sachqu] at-me, [those] lesser [tse'irim] in-days [le-yamim] than-I, whose fathers I-disdained [ma'asti] to-set [la-shit] with the-dogs of-my-flock [tso'ni].

**30:2** Also the-strength of-their-hands [yadeihem] — what [is it] to-me? Upon-them vigor [kelach] has-perished [avad].

**30:3** In-want [be-cheser] and-in-famine [kafan] they-are-gaunt [galmud]; they-gnaw [orekqim] the-dry-ground [tsiyyah], the-darkness [emesh] of-waste [sho'ah] and-desolation [mesho'ah].

**30:4** They-pluck [ha-qotfim] salt-herbs [malluach] by the-bushes [alei si'ach], and-the-root of-the-broom-plant [shoresh retamim] [is] their-food [lachmam].

**30:5** From-the-community [min gev] they-are-driven-out [yegorashu]; they-shout [yari'u] at-them as-[at] a-thief [ka-gannav].

**30:6** In-the-ravines [ba-arutsim] of-the-wadis [nechalim] they-dwell [lishkon], holes of-the-earth [erets] and-rocks [kefim].

**30:7** Among-the-bushes [bein sichim] they-bray [yin'aqu]; under the-nettles [charulaim] they-huddle-together [yesuppahu].

**30:8** Sons of-the-fool [naval], also sons of-no-name [beli shem]; they-were-driven [nikke'u] from-the-land [min ha-arets].

**30:9** And-now I-have-become their-song [neginatam], and-I-am to-them a-byword [lemillah].

**30:10** They-abhor-me [ti'avuni], they-keep-far [rachqu] from-me [mimmeni]; and-from-my-face [mipanai] they-do-not withhold [lo chasaku] [the] spitting [roq].

**30:11** For he-has-loosened [pittach] my-cord [yitri] and-afflicted-me [vaye'anneni]; and-the-bridle [resen] before-my-face [mipanai] they-have-sent-away [shillechu].

**30:12** Upon the-right [yamin] a-brood [pirchach] rises [yaqumu]; my-feet [raglai] they-push-away [shillechu], and-they-cast-up [vayyasullu] against-me their-ways [orchot] of-destruction [eidam].

**30:13** They-break-up [natsu] my-path [netivati]; they-profit [yo'ilu] from-my-calamity [le-havvati]; no helper [ozer] for-them.

**30:14** As-through-a-wide [rachav] breach [perets] they-come [ye'etayu]; under the-crash [sho'ah] they-roll-on [hitgalgelu].

**30:15** Terrors [ballahot] are-turned [hafakh] upon-me; [they] drive-away [tirdof] my-honor [nedivati] as-the-wind [ka-ruach], and-like-a-cloud [ke-av] has-passed-away [avrah] my-prosperity [yeshu'ati].

**30:16** And-now upon-me my-soul [nafshi] pours-itself-out [tishtappekh]; days of-affliction [oni] seize-me [yo'chazuni].

**30:17** The-night [lailah] my-bones [atsamai] pierces [niqqar] from-upon-me [me'alai]; and-my-gnawing-pains [orqai] do-not rest [lo yishkavun].

**30:18** By-great force [be-rav koach] my-garment [levushi] is-disfigured [yitchappas]; like-the-collar of-my-tunic [ke-fi kuttonti] it-binds-me [ya'azereni].

**30:19** He-has-cast-me [horani] into-the-mire [la-chomer]; and-I-have-become-like [va'etmashshel] dust [ke-afar] and-ashes [va-efer].

**30:20** I-cry-out [ashawe'a] to-you and-you-do-not answer-me [lo ta'aneni]; I-stand [amadti] and-you-stare-at-me [titbonen bi].

**30:21** You-have-turned [tehafekh] to-be-cruel [le-akhzar] to-me; with-the-might of-your-hand [be-otschem yadekha] you-oppose-me [tistemeni].

**30:22** You-lift-me-up [tissa'eni] to the-wind [el ruach]; you-make-me-ride [tarkiveni], and-you-dissolve-me [va-temogegeni] in-the-storm [tushiyyah].

**30:23** For I-know [yadati] [that] death [mavet] you-will-bring-me-back [teshiveni], and-[to] the-house of-meeting [beit mo'ed] for-all living [le-kol chai].

**30:24** Surely not against a-ruin [i] does-one-stretch-out [yishlach] a-hand [yad]; if in-his-destruction [be-fido] a-cry [shua'] for-them.

**30:25** Did-I not weep [bakhiti] for-the-one-whose-day-was-hard [li-qesheh yom]? [Did not] my-soul [nafshi] grieve [agmah] for-the-needy [la-evyon]?

**30:26** For I-hoped [qivviti] for-good [le-tov] — but-evil [ra] came; and-I-waited [ayechalah] for-light [le-or] — but-darkness [ofel] came.

**30:27** My-innards [me'ai] boil [rutchu] and-are-not silent [lo dammu]; days of-affliction [oni] confront-me [qiddemuni].

**30:28** I-go-about [hillakhti] blackened [qoder], but-not by-the-sun [lo ve-chammah]; I-stand-up [qamti] in-the-assembly [ba-qahal] — I-cry-for-help [ashawe'a].

**30:29** I-have-become a-brother [ach] to-jackals [le-tannim], and-a-companion [vere'a] to-the-daughters of-the-ostrich [livnot ya'anah].

**30:30** My-skin [ori] has-become-black [shachir] upon-me [me'alai], and-my-bones [atsmee] burn [charru] with-heat [me-chorev].

**30:31** And-my-harp [kinnori] has-become [vayehi] mourning [le-evel], and-my-flute [ugavi] the-sound of-those-who-weep [le-qol bokhim]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "dogs of my flock":** Job describes people so degraded he would not have employed them even as sheepdogs. The social reversal is complete — those beneath the lowest rung of society now mock him.

**v.9 — "their song and their byword":** Hebrew *neginah* and *millah* — Job has become the punchline and the proverb. The man who once silenced princes (29:9) is now the subject of derisive songs.

**v.19 — "dust and ashes":** The phrase *afar va-efer* echoes Abraham's self-description in Gen 18:27. Job's self-assessment mirrors the patriarch's humility before God, but here the context is despair rather than prayer.

**v.26 — "I hoped for good — but evil came":** This verse is the emotional center of the chapter, and perhaps of the entire monologue. It inverts the retribution principle: good deeds should yield good results, but for Job, the opposite has occurred.

*— EMET*
